judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the top-bar control that shrinks the text. It is a javascript:void(0) link with aria-label="A-", which overrides the image's good alt "Ícone - Diminuir Letra". The accessible name is just "A-". NVDA with default punctuation speaks it as "A", and nothing in its list item or the list gives the purpose programmatically. Sighted users get the visual A-/A+ convention; screen-reader users get a cryptic name. So the purpose (decrease font size) cannot be determined from the link text or its context. Borderline: some auditors would accept A-/A+ as a convention.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The visible link text "Español" in the language switcher is Spanish, has no lang attribute and inherits pt-BR. A change of language is clearly intended here, and the Understanding document's own language-link example marks each name with lang. So the visible text fails 3.1.2. Caveat: the link's aria-label "Link traduzir para Espanhol" is Portuguese and is what screen readers speak, so the mispronunciation the message describes mostly does not occur. The fix belongs on a span around the visible text, not on the link, or the Portuguese label would be mismarked. The mismatch between visible text and name is a separate 2.5.3 issue.
